speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you're presenting with hematuria and right flank pain. I need to ask you some questions to better understand your condition. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of recurrent urinary tract infections is concerning; do you have any history of kidney stones or abdominal trauma in the past? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance is Reddish. WBC is 10-20 /HPF. RBC is Too numerous to count. Nitrites are Negative. Leukocyte Esterase is Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The urinalysis confirms microscopic hematuria and sterile pyuria, which, combined with your right flank pain and lack of nitrites, strongly suggests a stone rather than a bacterial infection.
